chunk_findings.detail: The optional integer parameters are tested for truthiness instead of `is not None`, so zero is treated as “absent”. Given `FakeDigest().content_digest("x", length=0)`, the method returns a full 64-character hex digest because `return out[:length] if length else out` falls through to `out`; the same happens for `size=0` in the preceding truncation. Since the signature accepts `int` and the docstring says `length` cuts the hex, a caller asking for a zero-length digest gets a non-empty digest.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/fakes/__init__.py (FakeDigest.content_digest)

chunk_findings.detail: `lazy()` is a registration path, but it only honors `replace`, not `same_ok`. The class doc promises one duplicate rule: with `same_ok`, “the same definition again is a no-op.” Given `reg = Registry("kind", same_ok=True); reg.lazy("a", "mod:attr"); reg.lazy("a", "mod:attr")`, the second call raises `DuplicateName` even though the name and target are identical. This breaks the idempotent registration behavior `same_ok` is supposed to provide for lazy registrations.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/registry.py:lazy

chunk_findings.detail: Duplicate detection uses `have = self.table.get(name)` and then tests `if have is not None`, so a registered value of `None` is indistinguishable from a missing name. Given `reg = Registry("kind"); reg.register(None, "a"); reg.register(None, "a")`, the second call silently overwrites instead of raising `DuplicateName`; with `same_ok=True` it should be a no-op but also silently overwrites. Since `Registry` is generic and does not reject `None` items, this violates the stated duplicate rule; the check should use `name in self.table` or a sentinel.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/registry.py:register

chunk_findings.detail: The changed adapter tree still lists only `proc/`, `git/`, `fsio/`, `tomlcfg/`, `digest/`, and `forge/` as adapter homes. The 2026-11-01 correction under [D-adapters-answers-3] explicitly requires the doc to list the families added that day: MCP, ACP, agent lanes, lane transport, notify/ask, external tools, platform, log store, and secrets providers. After this change, a reader using this one doc to find the adapter homes will not see those required families, so the documented adapter model is incomplete and does not match the decision.
chunk_findings.title: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:219

chunk_findings.detail: The rewritten adapter model still makes `ddflow/adapters/ports.py` the place where ports are declared: the tree labels `ports.py` as "the Protocols", the prose says it "is the one module that gathers them", and step (1) of "Add a port" says "Declare the Protocol in `ddflow/adapters/ports.py`". That contradicts the operator decision [D-adapters-answers-2] that ports live next to their adapters in `ddflow/adapters`, and it also contradicts the same section's tree line `<family>/ ... with its port beside it`. A contributor adding a new port, for example `Search`, will follow the checklist and put the Protocol in the central `adapters/ports.py`, reproducing the pre-decision one-ports-module pattern the correction was meant to remove instead of placing it beside the adapter in `ddflow/adapters/search/`.
chunk_findings.title: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md — Adapter model / "Add a port"

chunk_findings.detail: The “shrink-only” fake baseline is not actually shrink-only. The test only asserts that every current port without a fake is present in `PORTS_WITHOUT_FAKE`; it does not prevent the literal from growing. For example, if a new port `MCP` is added without a fake and the developer changes the baseline to `{"Proc", "Git", "Fsio", "Toml", "Forge", "MCP"}`, then `missing == {"MCP"}`, `missing <= PORTS_WITHOUT_FAKE` passes, `PORTS_WITHOUT_FAKE & have` is empty, and `have <= set(_ports())` passes. The test therefore accepts a grown baseline, contrary to the comment and to the D-unify ratchet rule that ignore/baseline lists only shrink [D-unify].
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_ports_contract.py:test_every_port_has_a_registered_fake_or_is_in_the_shrinking_baseline

chunk_findings.detail: The new `ddflow.adapters.ports` module is only a 40-line module docstring; it defines no `Protocol` classes and has no imports/re-exports after the docstring. A concrete caller doing `from ddflow.adapters.ports import Proc` (or `Git`, `Digest`, etc.) gets `ImportError`, and any fake in `ddflow.adapters.fakes` that imports its port from this module fails at import. This contradicts the operator decision that ports live in `ddflow/adapters` and that every port exists for the fake ratchet.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/ports.py:1

chunk_findings.detail: The rename removes `ddflow/core/ports.py` with no backward-compatible shim in the manifest, so `from ddflow.core import ports` or `import ddflow.core.ports` now raises `ModuleNotFoundError`. This violates the change’s “no behaviour change for callers” requirement. The change explicitly keeps `ddflow.core.registry` as a re-export, but does not do the same for the old port path.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/ports.py (old import path)

chunk_findings.detail: The loader path is not atomic when `register` itself fails. For `Registry("thing", key=lambda _: "x", loader=lambda: [1, 2])`, the first `reg["x"]` registers `1` under `"x"`, then `register(2)` raises `DuplicateName`; `_ready` stays `False` but `"x"` is already in `table`. A later `reg["x"]` retries `_fill` and `register(1)` raises `DuplicateName` before the previously loaded value can be returned. `unregister("x")` cannot clear the entry, because it also calls `_fill` first and hits the same duplicate. This contradicts the comment “a failure registers none” and leaves the registry permanently unusable for that name.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/registry.py: Registry._fill_now

chunk_findings.detail: `lazy` does not honor `same_ok`. With `Registry("thing", same_ok=True)`, calling `reg.lazy("a", "pkg.mod:attr")` twice raises `DuplicateName` on the second call even though the target string is the same definition and the class doc says “same definition again is a no-op when `same_ok`”. The method always raises whenever `name in self.table` and `replace` is false.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/registry.py: Registry.lazy

chunk_findings.detail: Duplicate detection uses `have = self.table.get(name)` and then `if have is not None`, so a registered value of `None` is indistinguishable from a missing name. With `Registry("thing")`, `reg.register(None, "a"); reg.register(1, "a")` succeeds and silently overwrites the original entry, contradicting “registering a taken name is a `DuplicateName` error”.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/registry.py: Registry.register

chunk_findings.detail: The new setup excludes `"models"` and `"mcpshim"` from the loop that adds `"adapters"` to every layer, and the new test then re-asserts that exclusion. But the same test’s own comment says “Every code layer may import it.” A legal bottom-layer import in `ddflow/models/foo.py` such as `from ddflow.adapters.ports import Protocol` will be rejected by this guard, because `ALLOWED["models"]` never receives `"adapters"`. Since `models` and `mcpshim` are clearly treated as layer names by this very code, this contradicts the adopted rule that adapters sit below every code layer.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_layering.py (adapter ALLOWED setup / test_adapters_is_the_bottom_layer)

chunk_findings.detail: The test calls `PORTS_WITHOUT_FAKE` a “SHRINK-ONLY ratchet” and its comment claims “adding a name here … fails the test,” but the test only checks `missing <= PORTS_WITHOUT_FAKE` and `PORTS_WITHOUT_FAKE & have`. A change that adds a new port such as `MCP` to `ddflow/adapters/ports.py` and also adds `"MCP"` to `PORTS_WITHOUT_FAKE` in the same diff will make `missing == PORTS_WITHOUT_FAKE` and pass every assertion, because the new name has no fake and therefore is not in `have`. Thus the stated D-unify ratchet requirement that baseline ignore lists only shrink is not actually enforced.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_ports_contract.py:PORTS_WITHOUT_FAKE
